input.question: Why are some many comets peanut-shaped?
input.ground_truth: That's what you get if two roughly spherical solid objects approach each other slowly and stick together. [Ultima Thule](_URL_1_) is a good example, you can clearly see the two components. For asteroids near Earth we have enough data for statistics: [10-15% are contact binaries](_URL_0_).

Okay! Imagine a comet is like a big, dirty snowball that flies around the sun. But sometimes, instead of being round like a ball, it looks like a peanut!

The reason it looks like a peanut is because of how the comet is made and how it moves. Comets have two parts: a solid center (the nucleus) and a fuzzy cloud (the coma) around it. The nucleus is often not perfectly round. It can be more like a weird shape, kind of like a peanut or even a potato!

When the comet gets close to the sun, the heat makes the ice on the comet turn into gas and dust, which makes the fuzzy cloud. But the shape of the nucleus stays the same, so we see the peanut shape.

So, comets look peanut-shaped because their icy centers are shaped that way!
